sections.title: Medicine (system-wise, Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine style)
chapters: Cardiovascular system (ischaemic heart disease, ACS, heart failure, arrhythmias, valvular and rheumatic heart disease, endocarditis, pericardial and myocardial disease, hypertension, congenital heart disease, ECG)
Respiratory system (asthma, COPD, pneumonia, TB, bronchiectasis, pleural disease, pulmonary embolism, ILD, lung cancer, respiratory failure, sleep apnoea, ABG and spirometry)
Gastroenterology and hepatology (GERD, peptic ulcer, GI bleeding, IBD, coeliac, malabsorption, hepatitis, cirrhosis and complications, pancreatitis, jaundice, GI tumours)
Nephrology and urinary system (AKI, CKD, glomerulonephritis, nephrotic syndrome, UTI, renal stones, dialysis, renal tubular disease)
Endocrinology and diabetes (diabetes mellitus, DKA, thyroid, adrenal, pituitary, calcium and parathyroid, osteoporosis, obesity)
Haematology (anaemias, haemoglobinopathies, leukaemias, lymphomas, myeloma, bleeding and clotting disorders, transfusion, anticoagulation)
Neurology (stroke, epilepsy, meningitis and encephalitis, headache, movement disorders, neuropathies, myasthenia, MS, spinal cord, raised ICP, coma)
Infectious diseases and tropical medicine (typhoid, malaria, dengue, HIV, hepatitis infections, sepsis, TB outside the lung, antibiotics, tropical and zoonotic infections)
Rheumatology and connective tissue disease (RA, SLE, spondyloarthropathies, gout, vasculitis, systemic sclerosis, osteoarthritis, bone disease)
Psychiatry (depression, schizophrenia, anxiety, bipolar, substance misuse, delirium, dementia)
Fluids, electrolytes and acid-base disorders (sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, acid-base)
Emergency medicine, poisoning and critical care (shock, cardiac arrest, poisoning and overdose, snake bite, heat illness, ICU topics)
Oncology and palliative care (cancer biology, tumour markers, chemotherapy, paraneoplastic syndromes, palliative care)
Metabolic disease, nutrition, genetics and immunology (vitamins, inborn errors, genetic syndromes, allergy, immunodeficiency)
Other medicine topics, clinical pharmacology, ethics, evidence-based medicine, ageing, or junk rows

notes: Routing rules: 1) Rheumatic fever and valvular disease -> M1; infective endocarditis -> M1; hypertension (essential) -> M1, renovascular and renal hypertension -> M4. 2) TB: pulmonary -> M2, extrapulmonary and drug regimens -> M8. 3) Pneumonia -> M2; sepsis and tropical infections -> M8. 4) Hepatitis B/C virology and treatment -> M3 unless the question is about transmission/prophylaxis/epidemiology -> M8. 5) Diabetes, DKA, HHS, hypoglycaemia -> M5. 6) Sodium, potassium, calcium disorders and acid-base -> M12 (hypercalcaemia of hyperparathyroidism -> M5). 7) Anaemias, leukaemia, lymphoma, myeloma, bleeding disorders, anticoagulants -> M6. 8) Stroke, seizures, headache, neuropathies -> M7; psychiatric -> M11. 9) SLE, RA, vasculitis, gout -> M9; skin signs only -> M10. 10) Poisoning, overdose, snake bite, shock, cardiac arrest -> M13. 11) AKI, CKD, glomerular disease, nephrotic syndrome, UTI -> M4. 12) Tumour markers and cancer drugs -> M14; organ-specific cancers go with the organ unless the question is about oncology principles. 13) Vitamin deficiencies, genetic syndromes, immunology -> M15. 14) ECG, ABG, spirometry interpretation go with the system they test. 15) Use MX only if nothing fits.
